Inkal Awá, "people of the mountain", is a name the Awá use for themselves. They live in the rainforest on both sides of the border between Colombia and Ecuador, in Nariño, Carchi and Esmeraldas. They speak Awá Pit, a Barbacoan language related to those of the Chachi and the Tsáchila.

They live in scattered homesteads along rivers, farming plantains and maize, hunting and fishing. Roads, logging and coca growing have cut into their forest, and on the Colombian side they have been caught between armed groups in the armed conflict; Colombia's courts have named them among the peoples at risk of disappearing.
